_source: Star Citizen game files via StarBreaker
_assumptions: quality steps[].shareEstimate assumes rolls are integers drawn from a normal curve (mean, stddev) truncated to min-max; a band covers start-0.5 to end+0.5.

minedAt[].spawnShare (via belt) sums game-mining-spawns ores[].belts[].spawnShare over the location's rocks that hold the ore (rocks = how many); it is that dataset's estimate (see its _assumptions) and compares only between rows of one kind. slotShare is copied as is.
refinedBy[].processesEstimate lists every game-refining process for every refinable pair: no record ties a refining method to a resource.

qualityOverrideBelts: a quality location override applies to the belts of the star system it names (location "<system> System" or "<system>" against game-mining-spawns system); overrides naming a station match no belt, and belts without a system (Lagrange points, asteroid clusters) match no override.

cargo.kind: A small, wrapped package meant to get you in the Luminalia spirit. Banu merchants celebrating the holiday used to hide small gifts aboard their ship to encourage revelers to explore all their wares. As the holiday grew in popularity within the UEE, Human merchants modified this tradition by hiding empty gift-wrapped packages around a space station or landing zone that could be exchanged for credits if returned unopened. The increased foot traffic into their stores spurned holiday sales and became a tradition in its own right. \n\nStow this gift for sentimental value, or sell it at a commodities terminal and spend the credits on a holiday gift for yourself.

items.name: Special_HolidayLetter
items.type: A gilded red envelope celebrating the Year of the Dog. Exchanging these envelopes is one of the most popular ways of celebrating Red Festival. Often the envelope may include a small amount of credits inside to help those you care about have a strong start in the upcoming cycle. Growing in popularity is the newer tradition of hiding the envelopes as a way of spreading good fortune and prosperity to those that fate has deemed in need.
